epic_title: Kept for a later decision, not built now
summary: 23 capabilities the mapping surfaced but that are not built in this release, held in eight entries: a disabled note granularity, a configuration mechanism with no current second use, four calendar indicator sources nothing in the vault configures, the related-note list inside the date switcher, one interaction built on an undocumented Obsidian internal, one behaviour that should never be rebuilt at all, and mobile support. ICE-04 is kept as the record of a deferral that was reversed. Most entries cost nothing to defer; the exception is calendar sets, where the first release's data shape decides whether adding a second set later is a feature or a migration.

entries.title: Quarterly notes
entries.what_it_does: Adds a fifth note granularity, quarter, with the same create, look-up, enumerate, and settings-resolution behaviour that day, week, month and year already get: a user could open or create 'this quarter's note' from a configured folder, format and template, and the plugin would detect whether quarter notes are turned on. It would also replace today's dead 'Quarterly Notes' and 'Custom Notes' rows in Settings, which currently render as permanently-disabled, unclickable headings, with a real working section or remove them entirely.
entries.why_deferred: The user has quarter notes switched off in her live configuration, with no folder or template ever set for them, so nothing in the vault depends on this granularity existing.
evidence: vault: calendarSets[0].quarter has enabled=false, format='YYYY-[Q]Q', folder='', templatePath='' in the live periodic-notes-anks config — quarter is disabled and unconfigured

map: calendaric's own settings UI already ships a 'Quarterly Notes' toggle row that is permanently disabled with no expandable content, and 'Custom Notes' has no backing data shape anywhere in the codebase at all — both were UI scaffolding for a feature that was never wired up
entries.cost_rationale: Month and year notes are being built in this release with the same create/get/enumerate/resolve-settings shape quarter would need; once that generic per-granularity machinery exists, adding quarter mostly means adding one more entry to a config list and one more format/folder/template settings row, not new architecture.
blocks_if_omitted: NOTE epic: the note-granularity code (create, get, enumerate, resolve-settings, and the generic create-note dispatcher) must be written as one function per operation driven by a granularity list, not five hand-written copies or a switch statement naming day/week/month/year explicitly — otherwise adding quarter later means touching every one of those functions instead of extending a list.
SET epic: the per-granularity settings model and settings-UI row renderer must already be generic over 'whichever granularities exist' so a quarter row can be added without a new UI component.
entries.revisit_when: The user turns quarter notes on in her own settings, or starts wanting a genuine quarterly review note distinct from the existing Templater-driven '_04 1on1' folder, which already covers a quarterly-ish cadence entirely outside this plugin.
entries.risk_of_deferring: Nothing — no current note, template, or workflow depends on quarter notes existing.

entries.title: Multiple calendar sets
entries.what_it_does: Lets a user maintain more than one independent bundle of day/week/month/quarter/year settings — for example a 'Personal' set and a separate 'Work' set with their own folders, formats and templates — and switch which one is active from a command, a fuzzy-search quick-switch modal, or a settings dashboard listing every set as a card with add, duplicate, rename and delete controls plus a details page per set.
entries.why_deferred: The user's live configuration defines exactly one calendar set ('Default'), and her actual Personal/Work split is already handled a different way: a second physical folder, a separate template, and a ' - Work' filename suffix, not this plugin's calendar-set mechanism. There is no observed need for a second set.
evidence: vault: activeCalendarSet is 'Default' and only one calendar set exists in the live periodic-notes-anks config — multi-calendar-set support is unused

vault: the Work vs personal split in this vault is implemented ad hoc via a second folder, a separate template, and a ' - Work' filename suffix, not via periodic-notes' own multi-calendar-set mechanism — a merge should not assume calendar sets are how 'Work' is actually kept separate here
entries.cost_rationale: The CRUD UI (dashboard cards, a details page per set, inline rename, duplicate/delete with a last-set guard) and the switch-time side effects (re-run command and ribbon registration, reset the note cache) are a real chunk of settings-UI and state work on top of whatever the single-set v1 already builds — but only additive UI, not a data migration, provided the underlying config is already array-shaped (see blocks_if_omitted).
blocks_if_omitted: SET epic: the settings data model must store configuration as an array of calendar sets plus an 'active set' pointer (CalendarSet[] + activeCalendarSet), even though v1 only ever creates one set automatically — never as a single flat per-granularity settings object. Storing it flat now means a real data migration is needed the day a second set is added.

NOTE and CAL epics: every place that resolves 'the' folder, format or template for a granularity must resolve it through 'the active calendar set', not a hardcoded single settings reference, so switching sets later changes behaviour everywhere automatically instead of requiring each call site to be found and rewritten.
entries.revisit_when: The user wants a genuinely separate calendar configuration — different active granularities, formats or folders per context — rather than today's folder-plus-suffix convention, for example if she takes on a second, unrelated vault-like context inside the same vault.
entries.risk_of_deferring: If the SET epic's first release hard-codes a single implicit set instead of an array, adding calendar sets later becomes a migration of every existing user's settings JSON rather than a feature switch-on. This is the one item in this icebox where the architecture choice made now has a real, avoidable later cost.

entries.title: Extra calendar indicator (dot) sources
entries.what_it_does: Adds four more indicator sources for the small dots under calendar days and weeks, beyond the note-exists dot and the word-count dots US-CAL-07 builds: a streak source, a source coloured or labelled from the note's frontmatter tags, an unfilled dot when a note has incomplete task checkboxes, and a workspace event other installed plugins could listen to in order to register indicator sources of their own.
entries.why_deferred: The only dot sources the vault configures are note existence and the word count. No streak, tag or task indicator is set up in any readable plugin config, and no installed plugin tries to register one.
evidence: vault: the Calendar plugin's word-count-based heatmap dot (wordsPerDot) is the only dot source configured; no custom or metadata-based dot source appears in any readable config
entries.cost_rationale: If CAL epic's day-metadata resolution is built as a list of pluggable sources, even with only word-count shipped in v1, each of these three is a small, self-contained function of the same shape — a cheap store lookup for streak, a metadata-cache read for tags, a cached file read plus regex for tasks — and the third-party extension point is a thin wrapper over the same list.
blocks_if_omitted: CAL epic: the 'resolve per-day/week metadata' architecture story should keep the per-cell dot pipeline as an ordered list of source providers, not a single hardcoded word-count code path, so streak, tags, tasks and third-party sources can be added as new list entries later without restructuring how dots are rendered.
entries.revisit_when: The user starts using frontmatter tags or task checkboxes as a way to mark a day's status she wants visible at a glance on the calendar, or installs a third-party plugin that wants to contribute its own indicator.
entries.risk_of_deferring: Nothing — no workflow today reads, or would notice the absence of, these dots.

entries.title: Timeline complication (deferral reversed)
entries.what_it_does: Shows a small floating badge in the corner of any open periodic note with a relative-date label such as 'Today' or 'Last week' (plus an arrow if the note was only an inexact match); clicking it expands into a 7-day strip for jumping to a nearby day without leaving the note. It would mount and unmount itself automatically as markdown panes are opened and closed.
entries.why_deferred: Reversed. This entry deferred an active feature on evidence that did not say what it was read to say. The map observation reported only that no template, dataview query or note content references a timeline view, and flagged that a UI check was outside its scope. This entry turned that into 'enabled but unused'. TimelineManager is constructed on every plugin load, mounts a Timeline component into every open markdown view, and the component reads enableTimelineComplication, which is true in the live vault. The three capabilities moved to CAL and are built.
entries.evidence: obsidian-periodic-notes/src/main.ts:82 constructs TimelineManager unconditionally; src/timeline/manager.ts:14-63 mounts one component per open MarkdownView; src/timeline/Timeline.svelte:26-27,101 gates rendering on the setting; .obsidian/plugins/periodic-notes-anks/data.json:51 has enableTimelineComplication true.
entries.cost_rationale: It needs its own mount/unmount lifecycle manager reacting to workspace layout-change events across every open leaf, plus a small interactive UI component and the relative-date-formatting helper it depends on — a self-contained vertical slice, bounded but not trivial.
entries.revisit_when: Done — see the CAL stories that cover the three capabilities.

entries.title: Related-files switcher
entries.what_it_does: Inside the date switcher, a second list of every cached note related to the chosen period, optionally including finer granularities — every daily note inside a chosen month, for example — reached by pressing Tab, plus the count badge that shows how many such notes exist. The date jump itself is not here: it is US-CMD-10.
entries.why_deferred: The related-files list and its tab hand-off are a second surface inside the date-switcher modal, and nothing in the vault shows either being used. The natural-language date jump that shared that modal is not deferred: nldates-obsidian is installed and enabled, so that command does appear, and it moved to CMD.
entries.evidence: .obsidian/community-plugins.json lists nldates-obsidian among the enabled plugins, and obsidian-periodic-notes/src/main.ts:90-101 registers 'Show date switcher...' whenever that plugin is present. An earlier version of this entry claimed the plugin was absent; it is not.
entries.cost_rationale: The source material itself flags the hand-off between the two modals — closing one, opening the other, replaying the typed query via a synthetic input event — as untested, fragile glue, and its keyboard shortcut reaches into an unexposed, undocumented Obsidian modal internal (the private `chooser` field); building this well means redesigning that hand-off, not porting it as-is.
blocks_if_omitted: US-CMD-10 covers the date jump but not the count badge beside each suggestion, which needs this lookup. The badge is deferred with the list.

NOTE epic: nothing in the first release calls a 'list every cached note for a period' lookup, so it is not built. Adding it later must not require the note-lookup boundary to change shape — a period plus a granularity has to be enough to ask the question.
entries.revisit_when: The user wants to see, from the date switcher, what else exists inside a period — every day of a month, say — rather than jumping to one note.
entries.risk_of_deferring: Minor — grid-based navigation still gets her to any date; this is a convenience layer that today would depend on a plugin she doesn't run.

entries.title: Drag-and-drop note dragging
entries.what_it_does: Lets a user drag a day, week, or month cell's note out of the calendar view — for example to drop its link into another note, or the file itself onto another pane — using the operating system's native drag gesture.
entries.why_deferred: The only way to implement this relies on an untyped, undocumented Obsidian internal (app.dragManager) rather than any stable, public Obsidian API, and no vault evidence shows this interaction being used or needed.
evidence: map: calui:drag-day-or-week-note depends on an untyped, undocumented Obsidian internal (app.dragManager) — a fragile external dependency, not a stable API
map: dragging a cell with no existing file still starts a drag with the file undefined, with behaviour then entirely dependent on that internal's own undocumented handling
entries.cost_rationale: Correctness depends on an Obsidian-internal API that can change without notice across Obsidian releases, unlike every other cell interaction (click, hover, context-menu) in the CAL epic, which use documented public APIs — this one needs its own ongoing compatibility watch regardless of when it is built.
entries.revisit_when: Obsidian publishes a documented drag-and-drop API for file links, or the user specifically asks to drag a periodic note's cell into another note or pane.
entries.risk_of_deferring: Nothing lost by waiting — and building it earlier would not remove the ongoing risk of it breaking silently on an Obsidian upgrade, since that risk comes from the API it depends on, not from when it is built.

entries.title: Vault-wide loose date parsing fallback
entries.what_it_does: When no calendar set's configured folder-and-format matches a file, the old code falls back to guessing a date from the bare filename anywhere in the vault, using a loose regex for a YYYY-MM-DD-ish, YYYY-MM-ish, or bare 4-digit-year substring, and treats any match as if it were a periodic note.
entries.why_deferred: This is a defect, not a postponed feature. The fallback is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder, so any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose name merely contains a year, month or day-shaped substring gets miscached as an inexact periodic-note match. It should not be carried into the rewrite in this form.
evidence: map (P2 bug): 'the vault-wide loose date-fallback in cache.resolve() is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder... any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose basename merely contains a YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM/YYYY-shaped substring (e.g. "2026 Meeting Notes.md") gets cached as an inexact match for every calendar set that has active granularities, which can surface as incorrect +N related notes badges and pollute the related-files switcher with unrelated files'
entries.cost_rationale: If a scoped version is ever wanted, it is a small change: restrict the same regex fallback to run only inside a calendar set's own configured folder, reusing the strict-then-prefix matching FMT and NOTE are already building instead of inventing a new mechanism.
blocks_if_omitted: FMT epic: the date-parsing and note-resolution stories must not include a vault-wide, unscoped loose-match fallback; any 'last-resort' filename guess must be scoped to a calendar set's configured folder from the start, so this bug is not reintroduced by accident during the rewrite.
entries.revisit_when: Never in its current unscoped form. Revisit only if there is a real request for a folder-scoped loose-match fallback as a genuinely new, bounded feature — at which point it should be designed fresh against FMT's real parsing rules, not ported from this code.
entries.risk_of_deferring: None — leaving this out removes a source of miscategorized notes; no value is lost by not rebuilding it.

entries.title: Mobile support
entries.what_it_does: Running Calendaric on a phone or tablet.
entries.why_deferred: DEC-24 declares isDesktopOnly true for the first release, which stops Obsidian installing the plugin on mobile at all. Desktop first was the stated position, and one desktop-only call is what stands in the way.
entries.evidence: The guide-opening path calls an Electron API. DEC-03 already requires every desktop-only call to sit behind a single adapter, so mobile support means replacing that adapter, not reworking the views.
entries.cost_rationale: One adapter to replace, one manifest flag to flip, plus a pass over every hover-only surface. DEC-24 already requires those surfaces to have a pointer-free path on desktop, so that pass should find little.
entries.blocks_if_omitted: Nothing in this release. No story may promise phone behaviour while DEC-24 stands.
entries.revisit_when: The user wants the calendar on a phone, or the desktop-only call is gone anyway.

notes: pn:relative-date-humanization renders the label for both the Timeline complication and the date switcher. Both are now built, and it is covered by US-CAL-13.
ICE-04 covers nothing. It is kept as the record of a deferral that was reversed, so the numbering of the other entries stays stable.
